title: Los Pollitos Dicen — Unit 1 Home Supplements (Spanish Language Class Companion)

overview.description: A 7-slide PowerPoint parent companion for Unit 1 of a 'Los pollitos dicen' Spanish language program. Provides parents with: what to do at home to reinforce class lessons, unit vocabulary, and weekly practice guidance. The program uses 'living language' — students hear entire sentences in context instead of isolated words. Song-based learning is the primary method.
overview.philosophy: Living language acquisition through song and context. Young children acquire language by hearing words many times in different contexts. Most at-home practice is done through song.
components: Parent guidance slide (what to do at home)

parentGuidanceForLanguage.description: Slide 2 tells parents: 'Young children best acquire language by hearing words many times, in different contexts.' Then provides specific instructions: spend time several times a week, use the weekly checklist, reinforce through song. This is parenting coaching for language learning.
parentGuidanceForLanguage.value: Parents know WHAT to do and WHY. Not just 'practice Spanish' — specific methods backed by acquisition theory.

songBasedLanguageLearning.description: The program centers language learning around songs ('Los pollitos dicen' = 'The little chicks say'). Songs provide rhythm, repetition, and melody — all of which aid memory and pronunciation. This is the same principle as the ECME music education guidebook.
songBasedLanguageLearning.value: Music + language = natural pairing. Children learn songs without effort; vocabulary comes along for the ride.

weeklyChecklist.description: Parents receive a weekly checklist of reinforcement activities. This structures the at-home practice without being overwhelming.
weeklyChecklist.value: Accountability without micromanagement. The parent knows exactly what to do each week.

livingLanguage.description: Students hear entire sentences, not isolated words. 'Los pollitos dicen' teaches phrases in context: '¿Cómo estás?' not 'how = cómo, are = estás, you = tú.' Whole-phrase learning mirrors how children naturally acquire their first language.
livingLanguage.value: Natural acquisition over grammar drilling. Sentences before vocabulary lists.

gaps.name: language-home-supplement
gaps.description: A parent-facing companion for a foreign language unit: what to practice at home, how to practice it (through song, conversation, games), weekly checklist of reinforcement activities, and vocabulary reference. Designed for parents who may not speak the target language.

notes: Twelfth Aless drop. Second Spanish/language drop in a row — confirms foreign language is a priority for her. This is a CLASS companion (suggesting Aless may be taking or teaching a Spanish co-op class — 'Los pollitos dicen' is a popular Spanish immersion program for young children). The parent guidance approach (telling parents HOW to reinforce at home) mirrors the Harcourt School-Home Connection pattern Carolyng loved. Both parents want materials that bridge school/lesson time and home time.
